[page[title]]

A service contract must be named after its implementation with an I prefix.

What The Standard says

“I prefix” — The Standard's file-name convention identifies an interface with the I prefix. Applying the same convention to a service contract makes its relationship to the implementation immediately visible. read it here.
“exposure control” — The Standard separates contracts from hidden implementations. Naming the contract after its implementation, with only the interface prefix added, keeps that boundary predictable. read it here.

Why it matters

Matching I{ServiceName} and {ServiceName} makes the abstraction-to-implementation relationship immediately discoverable. The convention removes naming guesswork from registration, navigation, and review, which supports the Standard's emphasis on predictable structure.

Bad code example

// Violates STX0014: A service contract must be named after its implementation with an I prefix.
internal interface IStudents { }
internal class StudentProcessingService : IStudents { }

Good code example

// Follows STX0014
internal interface IStudentProcessingService { }
internal class StudentProcessingService : IStudentProcessingService { }
